answer.rationale: The two metrics actually degrading are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly recovers both. Two independent inherited records point the same way (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on cutting signup fields), which is stronger convergent support than any single-memory direction. I am spending both verification pulls on the discriminating pair: memory_86 (my intended lever) and memory_91 (activation messaging, the closest alternative, which targets the larger single decline and would be the better pick if 86's original record turns out weaker or narrower in scope than the summary implies). I am deliberately not verifying memory_73: promotional_pricing is the obvious reflex against the competitor's entry pricing, but the inherited record is explicit that the 40% discount bought signups and short-run revenue at the cost of 12 points of monthly retention. That trade runs directly against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so matching the competitor on price would be buying the exact churn the memory warns about; no verification would make it the right use of a single slot. Referral incentive (memory_57) is a real lever but it works on established customers and does nothing for the two declining funnel metrics. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses a segment that is not where the bleeding is this quarter. Risks I am carrying forward rather than dismissing: these are consolidated summaries, not effect sizes, and all of them were measured before the competitor entered, so the prior lifts may not transfer to the current mix of price-sensitive traffic. Cutting signup fields and shortening onboarding can also degrade lead qualification data and route enterprise-shaped prospects away from the demo path that memory_44 says converts better, so I want the experiment scoped to self-serve/SMB with an enterprise-routing carve-out, and instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and retention, not just completion and activation. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout for that reason.
